- **[2026-01]** Initial release of this repository, including the first set of Agentic MM-RAG papers. Ongoing updates will be added regularly.

## :house: About
This is a curated collection of papers on **Agentic Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic MM-RAG)**, an emerging paradigm that empowers AI systems to autonomously retrieve, reason over, and generate responses using multimodal information. By integrating external knowledge retrieval with agentic decision-making capabilities, these systems can handle complex, real-world tasks that require cross-modal understanding and iterative problem-solving.

This repository organizes recent advances in agentic MM-RAG framework design, evaluation benchmarks, and domain-specific applications, providing a comprehensive view of the field’s development.

This repository is regularly updated. Contributions are welcome during and after review; the public repository link will be restored in the non-anonymous version.

## Framework and Core Function
We summarize Agentic MM-RAG frameworks (listed in alphabetical order) and annotate their **Core Functions** during the agentic pipeline: Formulate (F), Route and Use Tools (RT), Verify and Correct (VC), and Stop and Budget (SB). **Mod.** specifies which stages involve modalities beyond text, including Query (Q), Corpus (C), Evidence (E), and Generation (G). **Learning** denotes the primary training paradigm, including In-context Learning (ICL), Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL). Please refer to our survey for detailed method descriptions, design rationales, and comparisons across settings.

## Evaluation and Benchmark
We summarize benchmarks across four evaluation dimensions: (1) **Retrieval Specification**, which assesses whether the system explicitly formulates step-level information needs; (2) **Retrieval Quality**, which evaluates whether appropriate sources and tools are selected and evidence is localized to correct citable units; (3) **Evidence Grounding**, which measures whether generated responses are properly grounded in retrieved evidence with accurate citation or alignment; and (4) **Stopping Optimality**, which evaluates whether the system terminates effectively under budget constraints by balancing marginal evidence gains against interaction cost. Please refer to our survey for detailed descriptions of these dimensions and benchmark works.
